items.title: Fighters sit too low with excess foreground mat
items.what: In all in-game and ready screens (e.g. images showing stance/technique sticks and fighters in white/red gis), the two characters stand in the lower third of the 3D viewport, leaving a large empty tatami floor area visible in the foreground below their feet and shadows.
items.why: On portrait phone (390x844 baseline), this makes the detailed photoreal fighters appear small (~35% screen height). Players immediately notice the distant, cramped action instead of cinematic close combat, reducing impact of the Three.js models and TSL bloom.
items.how: Adjust the Three.js camera position or FOV to raise the view angle and zoom ~18% tighter vertically so fighters' heads approach the bottom of the top HUD and feet sit just above the control UI. Rebalance the composition in the dojo scene.

items.title: Overwhelming direction labels above sticks
items.what: Gameplay screenshots (2,3,4,9,12,14) show a wide semi-transparent panel directly above the two large circular sticks that lists all stance directions (◀ step ▲ jump ▶ step ▼ crouch) and technique directions with icons, plus persistent STANCE/TECHNIQUE labels below.
items.why: The bottom ~30% of the portrait screen is visually noisy and text-heavy. New players cannot quickly parse the twin-stick mappings while focusing on the opponent, especially the patient AI that 'waits for your wind-up'. Hurts learnability and touch-first play in first bouts.
items.how: Make the full direction legend toggleable via the existing top-right MOVES button (hide by default). Simplify persistent UI to only show current stance/technique name or highlighted active direction. Increase stick hit area contrast.

items.title: Loading screen lacks progress indicator
items.what: First screenshot displays 'Downloading the game' in gold above a thin, completely unfilled horizontal progress bar on dark background, with static S logo, title, and 'A SHOEMONEY AI LABS GAME' footer. No percentage or animation visible.
items.why: This is the entry point. Without visible loading state (especially for WebGPU/Three.js asset download), players feel uncertainty or perceive a hang. Weakens first impression before reaching the warm dojo and fighters.
items.how: Wire the loader to fill the bar with animated gold gradient (matching title text). Overlay large, centered white percentage text (e.g. '42%') that updates live. Add subtle shimmer or pulse to the bar while keeping the cinematic dark aesthetic.

items.title: Hard-to-read AI behavior hint in qualifier
items.what: Qualifier screens (images 1,10,13) overlay white text 'PATIENT. HE WAITS FOR YOUR WIND-UP — THEN MAKES YOU PAY.' inside a dark translucent rounded rectangle, set against the dimly lit warm dojo background with volumetric lighting.
items.why: Low contrast makes the critical opponent tip difficult to read in the 2-4 seconds before the FIGHT button and countdown. Players enter the bout blind to the AI's counter style, leading to quick losses and frustration in the 1/5 qualifier round.
items.how: Increase the background rectangle's opacity or add a localized vignette. Apply a thin warm gold outline or glow to the text. Slightly enlarge the font while preserving the low-key cinematic tone. Test on device.

items.title: IPPON hit effects feel weak
items.what: In the IPPON screen (image 11), HasanAbi's spinning back kick connects with only subtle yellow streak particles/lines near Asmongold's head and a mild reaction pose; 'IPPON HASANABI SPINNING BACK KICK' text appears but the TSL post-processing doesn't emphasize the strike.
items.why: Scoring an ippon (full point, as listed in techniques menu) should feel rewarding and cinematic. The understated feedback fails to convey the power of the move or the 2½ point victory, diminishing satisfaction especially vs the patient AI on mobile where touches must feel precise.
items.how: Add a bright localized bloom flash at impact point, stronger screen-space impact lines or distortion, brief camera shake, and a red edge vignette on the receiver. Sync with existing film grain/vignette chain. Increase particle count for the kick.
